title: Dumbbell Stiff Leg Deadlift
overview: The dumbbell stiff leg deadlift is an effective exercise that targets the hamstrings, glutes, and lower back. This exercise enhances posterior chain strength, flexibility, andmobilityby focusing on hip hinge movement.Benefits include improved hamstring development, core stability, better posture, and increased athletic performance.Include this exercise in your nextlower body dayif you want to build lower body strength, improve flexibility, and enhance overall performance.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with palms facing your body.
Engage your core, keep your chest up, and your shoulders back. This is the starting position.
Push your hips back, not down, while slightly bending your knees. Lower the dumbbells along the front of your legs.
Continue hinging until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings (usually when the dumbbells reach mid-shin or slightly below.)
Reverse the motion by driving your hips forward, bringing your torso back up while maintaining a straight back. This is one rep.
Perform the desired reps, focusing on controlled movements and proper form.
tips: Maintain a straight back throughout the movement—avoid rounding your lower back.
Hinge at the hips. Push your hips back, not down, while lowering the dumbbells.
Keep the dumbbells close to your legs as you lower them.
